scope: Keep existing SDK heap capacity usable during slow VM operations and park longer contention through existing optional R4SYS notifications.

implementation.owner: Repositories/SDK/r4os/vm_allocator.zig; allocator_wait.zig is its private wait-channel helper. Default allocator and stable caller-owned Heap use the same implementation. No new module or kernel API.
implementation.vm: A monotonic per-heap operation ticket serializes VM preparation/retirement while the metadata lock is released around Reserve/Commit/Decommit/Release. A preparing slot and unpublished reservation remain private. Growth rebinds current boundary tags after completion, so concurrent allocation/free/resize below the committed boundary cannot invalidate a captured neighbor. Existing free blocks and eligible direct-cache entries remain usable.
implementation.failure: A retired tail keeps its exact region/offset/length until decommit completes. Failed unpublished-reservation rollback keeps its exact VM identity before another reservation. Direct release keeps a resident value descriptor and rejects the retiring allocation before reading its possibly unmapped header; accounting finishes exactly once after actual release. Cache retirement remains non-reusable after partial failure.
implementation.wait: Only a valid VM-capable table can become the canonical per-heap wait API; an unavailable startup context cannot leave a dangling or unusable first binding. Separate metadata-lock and VM-predicate channels observe revision before rechecking a predicate and parking. True metadata release, free publication and VM completion wake waiters. Exact referenced notification handles close outside allocator ownership; failed close retains identity for retry. Missing/partial optional slots fall back to sleep_ticks, then existing yield support.
implementation.lifetime: Caller retains an explicit Heap at a stable address through all concurrent operations and notification cleanup. VM call state stays on the current task's retained call stack; process-owned VM/notification namespaces keep existing exit cleanup. There is no new individual-thread cancellation API or new kernel unwind contract.
implementation.preserved: Size classes, alignment, boundary tags, coalescing, adaptive commit growth, small-region retention, direct-cache bounds, trim/OOM retry and public Stats shape remain. Fast frees do not acquire VM admission unless tail maintenance can be needed. Public platform and library contracts remain unchanged.

validation.host: 7/7 targeted VM allocator cases pass, including the original fragmentation/alignment/data/corruption/churn/failure/concurrent-thread and explicit-heap checks. One new grouped case pauses all four VM callbacks for both heap types, verifies free/resize progress and real host notification parking, then exact completion/cleanup. It also checks free-publication wake before another commit completes, pre-enrollment notify, missing/short optional slots, retained failed notification close and a partial direct release that erased its header. The existing failure group additionally checks retained unpublished rollback before reserve retry. Host VM and notification transport are models; production allocator/wait source executes directly. The same group rejects caching an unavailable VM table, then proves later binding to a valid table. This assertion failed on candidate SDK32 and passes after the SDK33 admission guard.

scoped_guest.scope: Existing CHECK MEMORY original cases plus one parallel SDK allocator group; real R4OS thread/VM/notification execution, default and explicit heaps, data/realloc/direct-region/cache/trim and actual joins before local cleanup. No broad Quick, pager/VM stress or benchmark.
scoped_guest.limits: Real thread concurrency on SMP4; not a claim that every worker ran on every CPU. Small-region virtual reserves remain until existing process cleanup. Host paused-callback/partial-error injection is separate.

prefinal_correction.result: Unavailable-VM-table cache regression reproduced:6/7 cases, then fixed by admitting only a supported VM table. Candidate build stopped after eight completed owners before any guest or STANDARD. Rebuild all139 on final SDK33.

source_audit.preserved: All policy constants and block/region/cache/Stats layouts; original free coalescence/accounting; actual Kernel artifact and source unchanged; SDK33 clean/published and archive identity verified.

comparison_previous.observation: Descriptive single-run comparison only. STANDARD does not directly time SDK malloc; no application-specific gain, parity or causal attribution. Keep all notable deltas and no score-selection rerun.

test_policy: Use the focused selector for the existing owner tests and one affected guest profile. No full host catalog, broad integration campaign or extra benchmark repetition. A new grouped regression case is needed for the unlocked VM/notification ownership boundary.
performance_policy: Mandatory final STANDARD because allocation and synchronization change. STANDARD does not directly measure SDK malloc; do not infer an application-specific gain from its score. Preserve workloads/reference and describe single-run changes without causal or parity claims.
limits: Host notification/VM models are not evidence of native scheduler or MMU behavior; the guest supplies separate execution evidence.
Windows and physical hardware are not exercised.
Explicit heaps retain their existing small-region reserves until process cleanup; zero active allocations is not a claim of zero retained virtual capacity.
